blocks.summary: Ran analysis on your current scenario. 'Carry on as now' was analysed as no change — the factors it compares against were held at the values your model records today. One limit on your model could not be checked: “Total initiative spend”. We could not line it up with anything this analysis measures, so it was not part of the comparison. The part of your model it points at is worked out from other parts, and Olumi cannot yet test a limit on a quantity like that, so it cannot be checked in this model yet; this one stays on the model unchecked. I supplied 25 of the values behind this, because your brief did not state them. They are mine rather than yours. Changing any of them changes what this model implies.

served_reply:
This run cannot put an option forward: the comparison is a near tie with very low robustness.

- These are model outputs, not forecasts.
- Small changes to the assumed links from feature-development spend to feature value, and then to paying subscribers, can change the ordering. That establishes fragility, not which assumption matters most.
- Both the £30,000 spend limit and the churn limit were checked only against Olumi estimates. The run also treated higher MRR as better; that objective direction is not yet recorded in the model.

No single option can be put forward yet, because a limit on your model was not shown to be met on this run, and running the analysis again as it stands will not change that; ask me what the limit needs before it can be checked.
